Define a count distribution for the regression functions

Source: R/user_families.R
new_count_family.Rd

Creates a count family from its log probability mass function, for use as family in countreg(), countreg_rp() and countreg_mix(). Only logpmf is required: the mean, variance, CDF and random draws are computed from it when they are not given.

Usage

new_count_family(
  name,
  logpmf,
  params = list(),
  mean_is_mu = TRUE,
  mean = NULL,
  variance = NULL,
  cdf = NULL,
  rand = NULL,
  valid = NULL
)

Arguments

name

a short name for the family (used in printed output).

logpmf

function(y, mu, par) returning \(\log P(Y = y)\) for vectors y and mu and a named list par of parameter vectors of the same length. Invalid parameter values should give -Inf or NaN (errors are also caught).

params

a named list of up to two count_param() objects. The first is modelled by dis_param_formula_1, the second by dis_param_formula_2. The coefficients are labelled ln(name), logit(name) or name, by link.

mean_is_mu

TRUE (default) if \(\mu = \exp(X\beta)\) is the mean of the distribution. Otherwise give mean, or the mean is computed by summing the PMF.

mean, variance

optional function(mu, par): the mean and variance. Without them they are computed by summing the PMF.

cdf

optional function(q, mu, par): \(P(Y \le q)\). If it has arguments lower.tail and log.p they are used, which is more accurate in the tails. Without it the PMF is summed.

rand

optional function(n, mu, par): random draws. Without it draws are made by inverting the CDF.

valid

optional function(mu, par): TRUE where the parameters define a distribution. Without it every finite value is accepted and logpmf must signal invalid values.

Value

An object of class "fcr_count_family".

Details

The family supports everything that needs only probabilities: fixed and random-parameter models, zero-inflated and hurdle models, finite mixtures, predictions of probabilities, quantile residuals, rootograms and simulation. Underreporting (binomial thinning) is not available, because a user family is not known to be closed under thinning.

The fit stores the family, so a saved model works in a new R session. Two families with the same name but different definitions are kept apart.

Use check_count_family() to test a new family before fitting.

Examples

# Negative binomial with size theta (variance mu + mu^2 / theta)
nb_theta <- new_count_family(
  name = "NB-theta",
  params = list(theta = count_param("log")),
  logpmf = function(y, mu, par)
    dnbinom(y, size = par$theta, mu = mu, log = TRUE),
  variance = function(mu, par) mu + mu^2 / par$theta)
# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
m <- countreg(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength, data = washington_roads,
              family = nb_theta, method = "BFGS")
summary(m)
